spec.name: rotate-first-fixed-skeleton-v1
spec.limitations: Rotation amounts are literal constants that never vary with data, so the bit-permutation skeleton of the map is fixed; an input bit difference keeps a rotation-aligned signature through the whole chain, and I expect the full differential table (which input differences produce which output differences) to be enumerable almost directly from the rotation angles. Also per-byte, keyless, and no cross-byte diffusion; the early rotations before any keying add no secrecy at all.
spec.math: Each step is a bijection on {0..255}: rol(n) is the cyclic bit-rotation with inverse rol(8-n); xor_c is an involution; add_c is translation mod 256 with inverse add(256-c). Nine bijections composed give a bijection, inverted by reversing order and applying the per-step inverse. The rotation sub-steps form a fixed bit-permutation group element on each byte independent of the data, and rotations commute with nothing here except themselves, so the skeleton is data-independent.
spec.assumptions: Byte-aligned input; per-byte independent application; rol is an 8-bit rotation with literal operand; operands are compiled-in constants, not externally supplied keys.
